results.title: Exhibition: A Life Composed: Chin Whai's Journey Through Music, Literature & Charity
results.description:
Born Tan Leng Gek (陈龙玉) (1938 – ), Chin Whai (秦淮) rose to prominence in the 1970s, when his songs captured the hearts of audiences across Singapore, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia. Known for his distinctive vocal style and deeply expressive ballads, he became affectionately known as the “King of Ballads”.

Yet, long before he took to the stage as a singer, Chin Whai began his career as a writer, with works appearing in publications such as Sin Chew Daily and Nanyang Siang Pau. He published his first book at the age of 22 and went on to produce 11 volumes of poetry, prose and essays. A prolific and versatile creative, he also explored the visual arts as a painter and illustrator.

After stepping away from the spotlight, Chin Whai devoted himself to giving back to society. Over the years, he headlined numerous charity events, using his music to raise funds and support those in need. His enduring commitment to philanthropy earned him another affectionate title—the “Charity King of Songs”.

Part of NUS Libraries Chinese Popular Culture Collection series, this exhibition celebrates the the multifaceted creative life and enduring legacy of Chin Whai through a selection of materials from his private papers, generously donated to NUS Libraries. Bringing together his writings, artwork, photographs and other personal materials, the exhibition offers a glimpse into the many facets of an artist whose creative journey has spanned music, literature and the visual arts.

results.title: Exhibition: Youth, Hope & Unity: Reflections on Pope Francis's Historic Visit to Singapore
results.description:
This exhibition documents His Holiness Pope Francis' visit to Singapore in September 2024 as part of his Asia-Pacific tour – including his address at the National University of Singapore's University Cultural Centre.

Featuring objects, photographs, video footage, and printed materials from the occasion, the display centres on the hand-crafted chairs used by Pope Francis and President Tharman Shanmugaratnam during the event.

The exhibition also presents replay footage of the Pope's address, selected publications from the Library's collection, and a section highlighting student-led interfaith initiatives at NUS.

results.title: RU+ A Scholar's World: The Life and Literary Circle of Chua Boon Hean 书香世家：蔡文玄生平与文人圈子
results.description:
The event will be conducted in Mandarin. AI translation in English will be provided.

Before Netflix, there was Shaw Brothers. And one man was at the heart of it.

Chua Boon Hean (penname Liu Bei’an, 1905-1995) was a renowned Singaporean poet, writer and cultural figure. He was among the 14 founding members of the Singapore Association of Writers in 1970, and his narrative poem Colourless Rainbow received the Singapore Book Council Award in 1978 and the prestigious Southeast Asia Write Award in Thailand in 1988.

Beyond literature, Chua spent more than three decades serving as the Manager for the Shaw Organisation in Singapore, overseeing film distribution, exhibition and even wrote film scripts for Shaw’s Malay film production. His family later donated his handwritten film scripts, annotated screenplays, and collection of rare books to the NUS Libraries, which became important resources for the study of Chinese literature, cinema, and popular cultures in Singapore and Malaysia.

A Scholar's World: The Life and Literary Circle of Chua Boon Hean explores Chua's life, career, and friendship, examining how his passion for literature, cinema, and the arts helped to shape the development and consumption of Chinese popular cultures in Singapore and Malaysia. Chua was also closely involved in establishing the connection, leading to Koh Siow Nam’s donation of over 7,000 volume collection to the University of Singapore Chinese Library in the early 1960s.

The programme features three presentations by one researcher and two librarians, together with a display of selected materials from the Chua Boon Hean and Koh Siow Nan collections. Through these rare manuscripts, publications, and archival materials, participants will gain a deeper appreciation of Chua's career as a “trans-media” cultural figure and how he weaved in and out seamlessly across the scholarly/literary field, business sector and the world of Chinese popular cultures in Singapore and Malaysia.

Programme


1.30pm    Registration
2pm         Welcome Address by Su Zhangkai
2.10 pm   Presentations

•    Tracing the Life, Career & Friendships of Chua Boon Hean 
by Dr Yap Soo Ei
A man of diverse interests, Chua spent more than three decades serving as the Manager for Shaw Organisation in Singapore and eventually established a “trans-media” career uniquely tied to the region. This talk traces his life, career and social circle. By examining his passion for literature, cinema, and the arts, this talk argues for Chua’s legacy in shaping the development and consumption of Chinese popular cultures in Singapore and Malaysia.

•    From Private Library to Public Collection: Chua Boon Hean as Catalyst in Koh Siow Nam’s Donation
by Dr Sim Chuin Peng
This talk explores how Chua helped facilitate the donation of Koh Siow Nam’s private library of over 7,000 volumes to the university library. Through personal trust, a timely suggestion, and his role as trustee, Chua became a key catalyst in bringing a private collection into the public realm, allowing its rich resources to benefit a wider community.


•    Chua Boon Hean’s Movie Manuscripts and Film Scripts
by Chow Chai Khim
At the turn of the 21st century, Chua Boon Hean’s children donated more than 400 movie scripts to NUS Libraries, most of which were written in the 1950s and 1960s. This session introduces this unique collection, which has attracted scholars from around the world and remains one of the most frequently requested special collections for viewing at NUS Libraries.

•    Q&A / Closing

3.30 pm Exhibition & Networking

 

Speakers:

Su Zhangkai (Moderator)
Honorary Library Fellow, National University of Singapore;
Associate, Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS)
Zhangkai is an educator and researcher in the fields of media, entertainment, and cultural history. He currently lectures at the SUSS and serves as a member of the Chinese Programme Advisory Committee under the Infocomm Media Development Authority of Singapore. He was previously a commissioned research fellow with the Hong Kong Film Archive and Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre. Zhangkai has authored and edited several works on film, opera, and popular entertainment history, including "Agak Agak – 90 Stories of Wang Sha and Ye Feng" (2019).


Dr Yap Soo Ei
Manager (Education and Youth Engagement), *SCAPE
Soo Ei works at *SCAPE, a non-profit organisation with a mission to empower youth in pursuing their interests and passion. Prior to joining *SCAPE, she was a research fellow at the National University of Singapore (between 2022 and 2025) where she assisted A/Prof Xu Lanjun in the setting up of a database on Chinese Popular Cultures in Postwar Singapore and Malaya as well as lecturing on a postgrad module “Chinese Diaspora and Mass Media in the 20th Century”.


Dr Sim Chuin Peng
Deputy University Librarian, National University of Singapore
Sim Chuin Peng holds a PhD from the National University of Singapore. He has been working at the National University of Singapore Libraries since 1993 and currently serves as the Deputy University Librarian. He specialises in the study of Ming-Qing history, Chinese publishing history, and Chinese bibliographical research. He has authored works such as Bridge for Success: Production and Circulation of Commercially Printed Examination Aids after the Mid-Ming Period, A Critical Examination of Ye Dehui’s Bibliographical Research, Revisiting the Bridge for Success: The Origins and Development of Commercially Printed Examination Aids, and has co-edited the Catalogue of Pre-Republican Chinese Books at the National University of Singapore Libraries (with Gao Bin). He has also published several academic papers in Mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan.


Chow Chai Khim
Senior Librarian (Special Collection Librarian), National University of Singapore
Chai Khim has served in the Library for over 15 years. As a Special Collection librarian, she is dedicated to promoting rare and special collections and supporting students and researchers in discovering related Chinese and English resources—particularly in the areas of Chinese Studies and Southeast Asian Studies. She also provides information services and develops engagement programmes. In her free time, Chai Khim enjoys reading and taking leisurely strolls with her toddlers around the neighbourhood.
